# E0339: type parameter of a function type that nothing uses

A function type's type parameter appears in its parameters or its result, so that each call can tell what it is. Delete the one that doesn't.

- Rule: [`polymorphism.function-types`](../../reference/07-types.md#polymorphism.function-types)
- Reported at: the type parameter.
- Tier: `advanced`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0339:1
fn first(f: fn<T, U>(T) -> T) -> i64 { f(1) }
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn first(f: fn<T>(T) -> T) -> i64 { f(1) }
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0339_type_parameter_of_a_function_type_that_nothing_uses.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0339_type_parameter_of_a_function_type_that_nothing_uses.lt):

```text
── TYPE PARAMETER OF A FUNCTION TYPE THAT NOTHING USES ── E0339_type_parameter_of_a_function_type_that_nothing_uses.lt:1:19  [E0339]

`U` appears in neither the parameters nor the result, so no call can tell what
it is:

  1 │ fn first(f: fn<T, U>(T) -> T) -> i64 { f(1) }
    │                   ^

A function type's type parameter appears in its parameters or its result, so
that each call can tell what it is. Delete the one that doesn't.

To fix it, delete `U`:

  1 │ fn first(f: fn<T, U>(T) -> T) -> i64 { f(1) }
    │                 ---
```
